title: Phase 3 acceptance specification — software acceptance vs experimental acceptance

referenceDocuments.note: Standard for Models and Simulations — guidance framework only; no clause-by-clause conformity assessment performed or claimed
implementation guidance; referenced for V&V terminology
Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement — uncertainty framework reference
Monte Carlo propagation of distributions — reference for the MC implementation
simulation-vs-experiment comparison principles (scope is CFD/heat transfer; used conceptually only)

softwareAcceptance.description: Infrastructure works: datasets import with provenance and QC, calibration is reproducible and detects non-identifiability, uncertainty propagation is tested, validation separation prevents leakage, evidence gating blocks synthetic data.
criteria: all Phase 3 unit tests pass on the CI matrix
dataset ingestion rejects malformed input, checksum mismatches, non-finite values, and unsupported units
synthetic fixtures are labelled synthetic-test-fixture and cannot unlock physicalValidation
calibration reproduces under recorded seeds and reports convergence and identifiability
non-identifiable parameter combinations are detected and reported without invented confidence intervals
calibration/validation split manifests are immutable and leakage-checked
physicalValidation stage remains none unless a real-measurement dataset with accepted quality meets prespecified criteria inside the demonstrated envelope

experimentalAcceptance.description: Requires genuine physical measurement data of suitable quality, acquired under the documented protocols, with instrument calibration records, prespecified criteria, and independent held-out validation observations.
experimentalAcceptance.status: NOT MET — no real measurement dataset exists in this repository
criteria: real-measurement dataset with complete provenance and accepted quality
prespecified validation criteria met within measurement uncertainty
validation dataset independent of calibration data (group-based split)

honestyRules: validation thresholds are prespecified before results are seen
a failed validation is a legitimate scientific outcome and is reported as such
calibration accuracy is never presented as independent validation accuracy
synthetic, analytical, numerical, or unknown-origin data can never support a physical-validation claim
no global physical-validity percentage; every claim is scoped to model + quantity + experiment + envelope
